rows.verified: HSE motor-vehicle-repair guidance covers mechanical repair, bodyshops, roadside recovery and electric or hybrid vehicles.
Two-pack isocyanate paints are a major cause of occupational asthma and can also cause dermatitis.
Powered discing and sanding can release high concentrations of hazardous fine dust.
Body filling and preparation should be separated from other work to minimise the number of people exposed.
Powered sanding and discing should use tools with built-in extraction or local exhaust ventilation.
Welding and other hot work should use suitable extraction, and extraction is especially important in confined spaces.
Vehicle lifts are lifting equipment and require thorough examination under LOLER at the applicable intervals.
Roadside repair and recovery controls must protect workers while also safeguarding other road users.
Motor-repair risk depends on vehicle technology, paint chemistry, repair task, lift condition, ventilation, traffic exposure and worker competence.
Motor-repair evidence is vehicle-, task-, chemical-, equipment- and location-specific and is not an exact parcel-level incident probability.
Printing businesses must manage machinery, fire and explosion, slips, manual handling, noise and dermatitis risks.
Printing inks, lacquers, adhesives, cleaning solvents and related products may contain substances hazardous to health.
Workers can inhale printing vapours and mists or absorb contaminants through skin contact.
Solvents and inks can cause dermatitis, while some UV inks and laminating adhesives can cause allergy or asthma.
Controls may include general ventilation, enclosure, local extraction, spill prevention, suitable PPE and good hand care.
Power-operated paper-guillotine operators must be trained and competent in machine risks, controls, safeguards and daily checks.
Printing-press safeguards must address significant mechanical hazards, including access during limited powered movement.
Health surveillance should be determined by risk assessment where inks, solvents, isocyanates or other sensitisers create health risks.
Printing risk depends on process type, ink and solvent chemistry, machine design, cleaning method, ventilation, access frequency and worker exposure.
Printing evidence is process-, product-, machine-, exposure- and worker-specific and is not an exact parcel-level safety probability.
